new.story: An Australian 50 cents from 1977, struck for Queen Elizabeth the Second's Silver Jubilee — twenty-five years on the throne. It is a big twelve-sided coin. The front shows the young Queen in Arnold Machin's famous portrait, the one Australia used through the sixties and seventies. The back is a celebration wreath: a shining starburst in the middle ringed by twenty-five little emblems, one for each year of the reign and for the states and territories of Australia, with the words SILVER JUBILEE and 50 CENTS around them. It was designed by Stuart Devlin, the goldsmith behind most of Australia's first decimal coins, and it was made to be kept — but plenty slipped into change anyway.
new.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Obverse: ELIZABETH II and AUSTRALIA around the Machin portrait on a twelve-sided flan; the date sits after AUSTRALIA at the lower right. Reverse: 50 CENTS and SILVER JUBILEE around a central starburst ringed with 25 small emblems, read off the photo in legend order. The year is design-locked: this Silver Jubilee reverse was struck for one year only, 1977, so the commemorative design itself settles the date even where individual digits sit soft in the photo. The twelve-sided planchet, Machin portrait and Jubilee reverse together admit no other Australian 50 cents issue.
